examples.solution_text:
On $0\le x\le3$, both curves are nonnegative. The outer radius is $9-x^{2}$ and the inner radius is $9-3x$.
$\begin{align*}V&=\pi\int_{0}^{3}\left[(9-x^{2})^{2}-(9-3x)^{2}\right]dx\\&=\pi\int_{0}^{3}(x^{4}-27x^{2}+54x)\,dx\\&=\pi\left[\frac{x^{5}}{5}-9x^{3}+27x^{2}\right]_{0}^{3}\\&=\pi\left(\frac{243}{5}-243+243\right)\\&=\frac{243\pi}{5}\ \text{units}^{3}.\end{align*}$

Find where the curves meet.
$\begin{align*}x^{2}&=3x\\x(x-3)&=0\\x&=0,\ 3.\end{align*}$
For $0<x<3$, $3x>x^{2}\ge0$. The outer radius is $3x$ and the inner radius is $x^{2}$.
$\begin{align*}V&=\pi\int_{0}^{3}\left[(3x)^{2}-(x^{2})^{2}\right]dx\\&=\pi\int_{0}^{3}(9x^{2}-x^{4})\,dx\\&=\pi\left[3x^{3}-\frac{x^{5}}{5}\right]_{0}^{3}\\&=\pi\left(81-\frac{243}{5}\right)\\&=\frac{162\pi}{5}\ \text{units}^{3}.\end{align*}$

The intersections satisfy $9-x^{2}=9-3x$, giving $x=0,3$. Their $y$-coordinates are $9,0$.
Rearrange the boundaries using their first-quadrant branches:
$\begin{align*}x^{2}&=9-y,\qquad x=\sqrt{9-y},\\x&=\frac{9-y}{3}.\end{align*}$
For $0<y<9$, the outer radius is $\sqrt{9-y}$ and the inner radius is $(9-y)/3$.
$\begin{align*}V&=\pi\int_{0}^{9}\left[(9-y)-\frac{(9-y)^{2}}{9}\right]dy\\&=\pi\int_{0}^{9}\left(y-\frac{y^{2}}{9}\right)dy\\&=\pi\left[\frac{y^{2}}{2}-\frac{y^{3}}{27}\right]_{0}^{9}\\&=\pi\left(\frac{81}{2}-27\right)\\&=\frac{27\pi}{2}\ \text{units}^{3}.\end{align*}$

Split at $x=5$, where the inner curve starts. Before $x=5$, the slices are discs with radius $\sqrt{x-2}$. After $x=5$, they are washers with outer radius $\sqrt{x-2}$ and inner radius $\sqrt{x-5}$.
$\begin{align*}V_{1}&=\pi\int_{2}^{5}(x-2)\,dx\\&=\pi\left[\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{2}\right]_{2}^{5}\\&=\frac{9\pi}{2}.\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}V_{2}&=\pi\int_{5}^{8}\left[(x-2)-(x-5)\right]dx\\&=\pi\int_{5}^{8}3\,dx\\&=9\pi.\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}V&=V_{1}+V_{2}\\&=\frac{9\pi}{2}+9\pi\\&=\frac{27\pi}{2}\ \text{units}^{3}.\end{align*}$

examples.derivation: On [0,3], 9-x² ≥ 9-3x ≥ 0. The squared-radius difference is x⁴-27x²+54x. Its integral is [x⁵/5-9x³+27x²]₀³=243/5, giving V=243π/5 units³. The shaded diagram closes along the correct straight-line boundary.
Solving x²=3x gives x=0,3. Between these limits, 3x is the outer radius and x² the inner radius. V=π[3x³-x⁵/5]₀³=π(81-243/5)=162π/5 units³. The diagram represents the enclosed region correctly.

The intersections are (0,9) and (3,0). For 0≤y≤9, the outer radius is √(9-y) and the inner radius is (9-y)/3. Their squared difference simplifies to y-y²/9. V=π[y²/2-y³/27]₀⁹=27π/2 units³. The first-quadrant diagram matches these boundaries.

The inner boundary starts at x=5. The disc portion gives π∫₂⁵(x-2)dx=9π/2. The washer portion gives π∫₅⁸[(x-2)-(x-5)]dx=9π. Their sum is 27π/2 units³. The diagram correctly includes the axis boundary before x=5 and the vertical boundary at x=8.
